channel.title: Jiǎoluò Shūwū · 角落書屋
channel.description: A reading nook for Chinese language and civilisation. Characters, vocabulary, grammar, history, philosophy, and the world they shaped.

item.title: 病 · illness, disease, to fall ill, fault
item.description: A person sweating on a sickbed with the phonetic 丙 inside: the radical 疒 frames every Chinese word for being unwell.

item.title: 春 · spring, springtime, vitality, the stir of desire
item.description: Sun pressing up through young shoots: the season of growth, and the oldest Chinese metaphor for life-force and erotic longing.

item.title: 哥 · elder brother, a familiar term for an older young man
item.description: Two 可 stacked into one glyph; the doubled phonetic came to carry the warmest word in the family, elder brother.

item.title: 馆 · a public building, hall, shop, establishment
item.description: A food-radical building: the eating-house that grew into the library, the museum, and the embassy.

item.title: 喝 · to drink; (hè) to shout, to cry out
item.description: A mouth radical paired with the phonetic 曷, splitting cleanly into the everyday hē you drink with and the older hè you shout with.

item.title: 河 · river, the Yellow River
item.description: 河 began as the personal name of one river, the Yellow River, before it widened to mean any river at all.

item.title: 湖 · lake, the provinces around Dongting
item.description: A water radical against the phonetic 胡, naming every still inland water from West Lake to the jianghu of wandering swordsmen.

item.title: 黄 · yellow, gold, the imperial color; to fall through
item.description: The color of loess soil and the emperor, of the mother river and the egg yolk, and the one color slang that means a plan has collapsed.

item.title: 活 · to live, to be alive, lively, work
item.description: Water gives the verb its life: a stream over a tongue, the flow that means being alive, and from there everything that moves, breathes, and gets done.

item.title: 鸡 · chicken, fowl, rooster
item.description: The simplified 鸡 swaps a chicken-coop hand 又 in where the traditional 雞 kept the sound-bearer 奚 beside the bird.

item.title: 急 · urgent, anxious, hasty, rapid
item.description: A heart pressed from above: 急 stacks a phonetic element over 心, so the glyph itself feels the squeeze of urgency.

item.title: 接 · to connect, to join, to receive, to meet
item.description: The hand that joins: 接 puts a wrist behind every link, every catch, and every arrival you go out to greet.

item.title: 街 · street, avenue, thoroughfare
item.description: The walk radical 行 splits open into a crossroads, and the jade-tablet phonetic 圭 sits inside, marking the place where roads cross and people pass.

item.title: 借 · to borrow, to lend, to make use of
item.description: One glyph carries both halves of a loan: 借 means borrow and lend at once, the direction settled only by context.

item.title: 离 · to leave, to be apart, away from
item.description: Once the name of a netted mythical bird, 离 was borrowed so long ago for to part that almost no speaker recalls its feathers.

item.title: 脸 · face, cheeks, social face, reputation
item.description: The flesh-radical face that doubles as a ledger of dignity: in Chinese you can lose it, save it, or tear it apart.

item.title: 练 · to practice, to train, to refine, skilled
item.description: Before it meant drilling and rehearsal, 练 was a verb for boiling raw silk soft, the repetition of treatment that hardens into skill.

item.title: 马 · horse, a common surname
item.description: A three-stroke pictograph of a horse in profile that hides the mane, legs, and tail of its towering ancestor 馬.

item.title: 牛 · ox, cow, cattle; (slang) awesome
item.description: A four-stroke pictograph of an ox head seen straight on, the horns still visible; in modern slang it means impressively good.

item.title: 朋 · friend, companion; of the same group
item.description: Two strings of cowrie shells hung side by side, an old unit of value, borrowed early for companions of equal standing who keep close company.

item.title: 热 · hot, heat, fever, ardent, popular
item.description: The four dots of flame beneath 执 carry physical heat into the heat of crowds, fervor, and whatever is trending.

item.title: 肉 · meat, flesh, the pulp of fruit
item.description: A pictograph of a meat slab with its marbling drawn inside; squeezed onto the left of a character it becomes 月, the flesh-moon of the body radicals.

item.title: 笑 · to laugh, to smile, to mock
item.description: Bamboo over a bending person: a form that has split scholars since the Song over whether laughter or rustling reeds came first.

item.title: 站 · to stand, to halt, a station, a stop
item.description: A person planted upright on the ground, holding their place: from the body that will not move grows the station, the stop, and the website you log on to.

item.title: 笔 · pen, brush, a stroke, writing
item.description: Bamboo over hair: the bamboo-handled writing brush drawn as a character. From the implement grow the act of writing, the strokes that build a glyph, and a measure word for sums and deals.

item.title: 表 · surface, to express, a table, a watch
item.description: The garment radical worn on the outside: 表 runs from the outer surface of things to showing feeling, the chart on a page, and the watch on a wrist.

item.title: 才 · talent, ability, only-then, not until
item.description: A sprout breaking ground, the first sign of growth. From that image grow two threads: talent as raw promise, and the adverb 才 that marks something later, harder, or smaller than expected.

item.title: 朝 · dynasty, imperial court, to face toward; (zhāo) morning
item.description: The sun rising among grasses with the moon still in the sky. From that dawn scene grow two readings: zhāo, the morning and its youthful vigor, and cháo, the court that met at daybreak, the dynasty it served, and the preposition toward.

item.title: 城 · city, city wall, town
item.description: A rampart of earth raised around a settlement: the character where the wall and the city it protects are one and the same word.

item.title: 传 · to pass on, transmit, spread; (zhuan) a biography, a commentary
item.description: The person radical carrying something onward: one figure handing a thing to the next. From that image grow the senses of 传, read chuan when it means to pass down, transmit, and spread, and read zhuan when it names a biography or a classical commentary.
